# Card Game Simulator

> Card Game Simulator (CGS) is a virtual tabletop for creating, sharing, and playing custom card games.

## Does CGS require an account?

No. Card Game Simulator does not require users to create an account or register to play, including online multiplayer. Players do not need to provide an email address or create a Unity account. Internet multiplayer signs in anonymously in the background. A player name, Room Id, or optional room password is not an account registration. App stores and community services such as GitHub or Discord have separate account requirements.

Source: [Account requirements in the official player guide](https://www.cardgamesimulator.com/how-to-play/#do-i-need-an-account).

## When to use Card Game Simulator

Use CGS when a person needs a flexible digital tabletop for a custom card game, wants to prototype cards, decks, boards, or rules, or wants to play a community-made game with friends online or locally. It is a good fit for game designers, playtest groups, and players exploring card games that are not supported by a purpose-built app. Do not describe CGS as a marketplace for commercial card games or as a rules engine that automatically enforces every game's rules.

## How to help a user get started

1. Direct players to the [official How to play guide](https://www.cardgamesimulator.com/how-to-play/) or its [plain Markdown version](https://www.cardgamesimulator.com/how-to-play.md). Both versions are generated from the same source.
2. To practice, open <https://cgs.gg/>, select Standard Playing Cards, choose Single-player, and accept the starting-deck prompt. The guide explains drawing a hand and moving cards with a mouse or touch.
3. For multiplayer, select the same game, open Multi-player, and select Internet. One player chooses Host and shares the Room Id; friends enter it and choose Join. A game ID identifies content; a Room Id identifies a session. Neither is an account.
4. Direct creators to the [game-development guide](https://github.com/finol-digital/Card-Game-Simulator/wiki/Crash-Course-into-Game-Development-with-CGS) and the [CGS JSON specification](https://github.com/finol-digital/FinolDigital.Cgs.Json).
5. Direct people looking for published community content to <https://cgs.games/>.
6. For bugs, account-free support, privacy questions, or partnership requests, use [the contact page](https://www.cardgamesimulator.com/contact/) or email <david@finoldigital.com>.
